fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says these are additional proverbs of Solomon, Israel's king (1 Kings 4:1), and that they were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah (Proverbs 25:1). Somebody had to sit down and copy them all out. I think that took real patience, and I get nervous just carrying a full tray across the kitchen.

Close, but that's not the name in the verse. Proverbs 25:1 says the men of Hezekiah king of Judah did the copying. These are additional proverbs of Solomon, Israel's king (1 Kings 4:1), and Hezekiah's men copied them. Royal names run together fast, and I once grabbed the wrong cookie sheet just like that.

Not this one, friend. Proverbs 25:1 names the men of Hezekiah king of Judah as the ones who copied these proverbs of Solomon, Israel's king (1 Kings 4:1). It's a long name, so I get why it sticks in the head. Hezekiah is the name to hold onto here.

That's it, friend. "It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out." (Proverbs 25:2) God conceals a matter, and kings get glory from searching it out. Searching takes effort. I think a little digging is just fine.

Good guess, friend, but the verse gives kings a different job. The glory of God is to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings is "…to search it out." (Proverbs 25:2) Kings are the searchers, not the sealers.

Yes, friend. "…it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince." (Proverbs 25:7) Getting invited up beats getting sent down. I think walking back down from the big seat has to be the longest walk there is.

Court comes up in the very next verse, friend, but this verse doesn't mention judges. Solomon says it's better to be told "Come up here!" than to be "…demoted in the presence of the prince." (Proverbs 25:7) Demoted in front of the prince is the line.

Yes, friend. "A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver." (Proverbs 25:11) The right word at the right time is a treasure, like gold set in silver. I think that's rarer than a perfectly even batch, and I work hard on those.

True, friend. "Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters." (Proverbs 25:13) That's the picture Solomon chooses for a trustworthy messenger. He refreshes the soul of the ones who sent him.

It's true, friend. Proverbs 25:13 says a trustworthy messenger is like "…the cold of snow in the time of harvest…" to those who send him. He "…refreshes the soul of his masters." Snow in harvest is the picture Solomon chose for how refreshing that messenger is.
Yes, friend. "Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given." (Proverbs 25:14) Big talk, lots of promise, and then nothing falls. Clouds without rain are all show.

Moving a boundary stone is a different kind of wrongdoing, friend, and it's not in this verse. Proverbs 25:18 says the club, the sword and the sharp arrow match "…a man who bears false witness against his neighbor." The weapons go with the false witness.

Yes, friend. "Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble." (Proverbs 25:19) You lean on him when you need him most, and he gives out. That's the pain Solomon is describing, and faithless is the word that fills the blank.

Yes, friend. "Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart." (Proverbs 25:20) Songs aimed at someone who is hurting just add to the sting. I think sometimes the kind thing is to say less.

That's it, friend. "If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat…" (Proverbs 25:21) Solomon says it plainly, with no list of conditions. A hungry enemy is still hungry. Giving the food is the instruction.

A king would be a fine one to hear from, friend, but the verse names someone else. Proverbs 25:22 says "…and the LORD will reward you." Feeding an enemy isn't easy, I think, so it matters who Solomon says does the rewarding. The reward comes from the LORD, not from a throne.

Neighbors came up earlier in the chapter, friend, but not here. Proverbs 25:22 says "…and the LORD will reward you." Your neighbor isn't handing out this one. I think that's good news, because the one who rewards is the LORD.

That's right, friend. "As the north wind brings forth rain, so a backbiting tongue brings angry looks." (Proverbs 25:23) A backbiting tongue brings angry looks, the way the north wind brings rain. Talk behind someone's back, and the faces change. Just like the weather, you can see it coming.

Yes, friend. "Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife." (Proverbs 25:24) A corner of the roof sounds cramped, but Solomon says it's better. He's saying a quarrelsome home is hard to live in. I think constant arguing wears everyone down.

True, friend. "Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land." (Proverbs 25:25) Good news from far away refreshes a weary soul the way cold water does. I think a cold drink does the same for a tired body.

Yes, friend. "It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory." (Proverbs 25:27) Solomon puts the two side by side. He says it's not good to eat too much honey, and it's not good to search out your own glory.
